thread:
ana: Trying the quickstart inside a k8s pod (minikube) and my first outbound request is returning a 502 HTML page. Same token works from the dashboard. any ideas?

ana: command I ran: `kubectl run quickstart-test --image=sample/quickstart --env=REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY --rm -it --restart=Never --command -- /bin/sh -c \"node index.js\"`

ana: output:
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer ***
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\ncontent-type: text/html\n\n<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

keith: is that a workspace token or a service key? 502 usually points to some proxy or gateway.

ana: it's a workspace token created in the Console. I tried a service key too — that gave me 403 error from the API. workspace token -> 502.

infra-bot: Note: Some corporate sidecars and cluster ingress controllers strip Authorization headers. If header is removed, the SDK may retry and trigger a different upstream path.

ana: interestingly when I run `curl` from my laptop with the same workspace token I get a clear 402 JSON: `{"error":"org_billing_required"}`. inside k8s it's the HTML 502.

keith: that indicates header removal on the pod/network path. Also the dashboard quickstart can appear to succeed locally because it hits the control plane which returns a different UI flow. mismatch between control plane UX and actual org billing state is causing confusion.

onboard-bot: Heads up: Your org (acme-dev) is missing a billing method. First outbound calls may be gated until billing is added. Console: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/acme-dev/billing :credit_card:

ana: reproducible steps: 1) org without billing method 2) create workspace token 3) run quickstart inside cluster/proxy that strips Authorization 4) observe 502 instead of 402.

keith: proposed fixes: 1) CLI/SDK should surface a clearer message when upstream 502s match known header-strip patterns (map to billing-required hint). 2) Add a preflight call in the CLI quickstart that checks org billing status and warns before making outbound requests. 3) docs: note common k8s ingress and sidecar configs that drop Authorization.

infra-bot: Workaround: mount a service key file into the pod and set REDWOOD_API_KEY by reading the file at runtime (bypass some proxy rewrites), or use an image that performs the token handshake over TLS directly from the pod.

ana: confirmed workaround: `kubectl run quickstart-test --image=sample/quickstart --env=REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.redwood/service_key) ...` returned JSON 402 with `org_billing_required`.

keith: I'll log an eng/devex ticket with the minimal k8s manifest, ingress rules, `kubectl` command, and curl traces. we should also consider making the SDK stop retrying on connection errors that are likely header/body mismatches to avoid obscure 502s.

ana: filing issue now and attaching network capture + container logs. cc @keith. thanks for the triage! :pray:
